literature.note: Slower than the 3-5 cm/yr target, but this semi-arid Mediterranean basin should have good coherence. Hotspots sit on fine sediments with a falling shallow water table, and in cropland with excess water withdrawal. GNSS shows about 10 mm/yr of regional tectonic uplift, so relative rates are what matter. Olea et al. 2020 (ISPRS Archives XLII-3/W12, doi 10.5194/isprs-archives-XLII-3-W12-2020-1-2020; DOI not checked on Crossref) report up to 28 mm/yr (LOS velocity) in a NW Santiago industrial area for 2017-2018, interpreted as groundwater exploitation. The centre is approximate (NW Santiago, Pudahuel/Quilicura) and needs review against the published maps.

lost_hills.name: Lost Hills & Belridge oil fields, California

literature.quantity: line of sight?

literature.citation: Fielding E.J., Blom R.G., Goldstein R.M. (1998). Rapid subsidence over oil fields measured by SAR interferometry. Geophysical Research Letters 25(17), 3215-3218.
literature.note: Abstract: 'Maximum subsidence rates are as high as 40 mm in 35 days or >400 mm/yr'. This is a peak short-interval rate, not a long-term mean, and the abstract does not say whether it is LOS or vertical. Patzek & Silin report a Belridge maximum of ~0.8-1 ft/yr (1988-99). No Sentinel-era source was found, and current rates are probably lower because of waterflooding. The centre, between Lost Hills (~35.62N) and South Belridge (~35.45N), is OK. Reference: needs review (the nearby hills are oil-bearing Tertiary sediments).

literature.quantity: vertical (GNSS)
literature.period: ~2008-2017 (almost 10 years of CGNSS, up to autumn 2017)
literature.citation: Argyrakis, P., Ganas, A., Valkaniotis, S., Tsioumas, V., Sagias, N., Psiloglou, B. (2020). Anthropogenically induced subsidence in Thessaly, central Greece: new evidence from GNSS data. Natural Hazards 102, 179-200.
literature.note: Verified abstract statement: the vertical GNSS series at STEF (Stefanovikeio, Karla area, about 39.47N 22.74E) reaches a cumulative 55 cm. The Larissa (LARM) and Karditsa stations show no net subsidence. No per-year rate was found in accessible text, so rate_cm_yr is null; 55 cm over about 10 years would imply about 5 cm/yr, but that is not verified. Older PSI (Envisat) gave up to -25 mm/yr around Larissa. No peer-reviewed Sentinel-1 rate was found. Antoniadis & Loupasakis 2025 (Land 14:827, doi 10.3390/land14040827) is an InSAR review of East Thessaly; its full text may give one. Reading the EGMS vertical product for the Karla basin directly is another option.

reference.reason: pre-Quaternary bedrock south of city; 2025 paper shows the southern area stable or slightly uplifting

literature.quantity: vertical (asc+desc P-SBAS Sentinel-1)
literature.citation: Navarro, A.M.G., Eid, C., Rocca, V., Benetatos, C., De Luca, C., Onorato, G., Lanari, R. (2025). Integrated Analysis of Satellite and Geological Data to Characterize Ground Deformation in the Area of Bologna (Northern Italy) Using a Cluster Analysis-Based Approach. Remote Sensing 17(15), 2645.
literature.note: The paper gives no peak rate. It states 'net displacement of up to -68 mm (cluster 1) over the investigated period (June 2016-October 2021)' in the high-pumping Bologna area. That is about 1.3 cm/yr as a cluster average (our arithmetic). The 1970s peak was about 10 cm/yr (Zuccarini et al. 2024, BEGE, doi 10.1007/s10064-023-03517-5), and 1992-2000 rates reached up to 59 mm/yr NE of the city. In the 2025 paper the southern area shows slight uplift (up to 2 mm/yr), which supports using it as the reference. The draft's 3 cm/yr is too high for 2016-2021.
